abstract_html: '<p>On a discrete grid several curves may cross and share cells, yet a tracer following one curve must recover, at every shared cell, where ITS OWN curve continues. We ask for a single static number per cell --- no stored lists --- from which each curve reads its next step with no collision. The answer is to read the cell number as a member of a SEPARATING FAMILY: assign curve i the prime p_i and store the product of p_i raised to curve i''s local Freeman direction; each curve recovers its direction as the exponent of its own prime, and unique factorisation guarantees that distinct curves never interfere.</p><p>We analyse the cost of this prime code and give more compact separating families --- the residue number system (Chinese Remainder Theorem), positional mixed-radix, and bit-packing --- that share the same properties without factorisation; the prime form is space-dominated. The result is sharp: a local, state-blind tracer cannot resolve a tangency (two curves entering a cell alike but leaving differently) by any cell number, so the irreducible resource is a per-curve index, of order log m bits, carried in the tracer, not in the cell (the local-indistinguishability theorem). The construction has a mutable dual: the rotor-router places the same disambiguating resource inside the cell and advances it on each visit. Separating family and rotor-router are the two escapes of the impossibility boundary. Simple curves --- open paths, closed loops, and rho-shapes --- are admissible; only genuine self-intersection is excluded, with a branch-separation (residue-jet) extension outlined for it.</p><p>An interactive demonstration runs at https://l3ragio.github.io/one-number-per-cell/ (source: https://github.com/l3ragio/one-number-per-cell).</p>'
